_about: Hand-written instruction reference data (TASK-092). Pages Content/Reference/instructions-*.txt are generated from this file and the engine's opcode table by ReferenceTests (set ASSEMBLY_STUDIO_WRITE_REFERENCE=1 to regenerate). 'modified' and 'undefined' are checked against the engine by running 'probe' from random states (AC-037).

instructions.name: Move
instructions.operation: Copies the source to the destination: destination = source.
instructions.notes: There is no memory-to-memory form, and no form that loads a constant straight into a segment register: go through a general register.

instructions.name: Exchange
instructions.operation: Swaps the two operands.
instructions.notes: XCHG AX, AX is the same byte as NOP (90h).

instructions.name: Push a word onto the stack
instructions.operation: SP = SP - 2, then the word is stored at SS:SP.
instructions.notes: Only words can be pushed. PUSH SP stores the value SP has after the decrement (8086 behavior).

instructions.name: Pop a word from the stack
instructions.operation: The word at SS:SP is copied to the destination, then SP = SP + 2.
instructions.notes: POP CS (0Fh) is not supported.

instructions.name: Push the flags
instructions.operation: Pushes the FLAGS register.
instructions.notes: Together with POP this is how a program reads all the flags (as in the arithmetic-flags sample).

instructions.name: Pop the flags
instructions.operation: Pops a word into the FLAGS register.
instructions.notes: Every flag takes the value of its bit in the popped word.

instructions.name: Load AH from the flags
instructions.operation: AH = the low byte of FLAGS (SF, ZF, AF, PF and CF).

instructions.name: Store AH into the flags
instructions.operation: The low byte of FLAGS = AH.
instructions.notes: OF is in the high byte, so SAHF can't change it.

instructions.name: Load effective address
instructions.operation: Puts the offset of the memory operand in a register, without reading memory.
instructions.notes: Handy for adding registers and constants: lea ax, [bx + si + 4] computes BX + SI + 4.

instructions.name: Load pointer using DS
instructions.operation: Reads a far pointer from memory: the register gets the offset (first word), DS the segment (second word).

instructions.name: Load pointer using ES
instructions.operation: Like LDS, but loads ES.

instructions.name: Translate with a table
instructions.operation: AL = the byte at DS:[BX + AL].
instructions.notes: BX points at a table of up to 256 bytes; AL is the index.

instructions.name: Add
instructions.operation: destination = destination + source.
instructions.notes: CF reports an unsigned carry out of the top bit; OF reports a signed result that doesn't fit.

instructions.name: Add with carry
instructions.operation: destination = destination + source + CF.
instructions.notes: Adds numbers wider than 16 bits: ADD the low words, then ADC the high words.

instructions.name: Subtract
instructions.operation: destination = destination - source.
instructions.notes: CF is set when a borrow is needed (the unsigned source is larger).

instructions.name: Subtract with borrow
instructions.operation: destination = destination - source - CF.
instructions.notes: Subtracts numbers wider than 16 bits, like ADC adds them.

instructions.name: Compare
instructions.operation: Computes destination - source and sets the flags like SUB, but keeps neither result.
instructions.notes: Usually followed by a conditional jump.

instructions.name: Increment
instructions.operation: destination = destination + 1.
instructions.notes: Unlike ADD, INC leaves CF unchanged.

instructions.name: Decrement
instructions.operation: destination = destination - 1.
instructions.notes: Unlike SUB, DEC leaves CF unchanged. DEC followed by JNZ makes a counting loop.

instructions.name: Negate
instructions.operation: destination = 0 - destination (two's complement).
instructions.notes: CF is set unless the operand was 0.

instructions.name: Unsigned multiply
instructions.operation: Byte: AX = AL * source. Word: DX:AX = AX * source.
instructions.notes: OF and CF are set when the upper half of the result (AH or DX) isn't 0.

instructions.name: Signed multiply
instructions.operation: Like MUL, for signed numbers.
instructions.notes: OF and CF are set when the upper half isn't just the sign extension of the lower half. The 8086 has only the one-operand form.

instructions.name: Unsigned divide
instructions.operation: Byte: AL = AX / source, AH = remainder. Word: AX = DX:AX / source, DX = remainder.
instructions.notes: Dividing by 0, or a quotient too big for AL or AX, raises a divide error (interrupt 0), which stops the program with a runtime error.

instructions.name: Signed divide
instructions.operation: Like DIV, for signed numbers; the remainder has the sign of the dividend.
instructions.notes: Divide errors as for DIV. Use CBW or CWD first to sign-extend the dividend.

instructions.name: Convert byte to word
instructions.operation: AH = 00h if AL is positive, FFh if negative (sign extension of AL into AX).

instructions.name: Convert word to double word
instructions.operation: DX = 0000h if AX is positive, FFFFh if negative (sign extension of AX into DX:AX).

instructions.name: Decimal adjust after addition
instructions.operation: Corrects AL after adding two packed BCD bytes (two decimal digits per byte).

instructions.name: Decimal adjust after subtraction
instructions.operation: Corrects AL after subtracting two packed BCD bytes.

instructions.name: ASCII adjust after addition
instructions.operation: Corrects AL after adding two unpacked BCD digits; a carry goes into AH.

instructions.name: ASCII adjust after subtraction
instructions.operation: Corrects AL after subtracting two unpacked BCD digits; a borrow comes from AH.

instructions.name: ASCII adjust after multiplication
instructions.operation: AH = AL / 10, AL = AL mod 10 (splits a number below 100 into two digits).
instructions.notes: The divisor is the byte after the opcode (10 when written as plain AAM). A divisor of 0 raises a divide error.

instructions.name: ASCII adjust before division
instructions.operation: AL = AH * 10 + AL, AH = 0 (joins two digits into one number).

instructions.name: Logical AND
instructions.operation: Each result bit is 1 when both operand bits are 1.
instructions.notes: OF and CF are always cleared. Use it to clear bits: and al, 0Fh keeps the low four bits.

instructions.name: Logical OR
instructions.operation: Each result bit is 1 when either operand bit is 1.
instructions.notes: OF and CF are always cleared. Use it to set bits: or al, 20h makes an ASCII letter lower case.

instructions.name: Logical exclusive OR
instructions.operation: Each result bit is 1 when the operand bits differ.
instructions.notes: OF and CF are always cleared. xor ax, ax is a common way to set AX to 0.

instructions.name: Logical NOT
instructions.operation: Inverts every bit (one's complement).

instructions.name: Test bits
instructions.operation: ANDs the operands and sets the flags like AND, but keeps no result.
instructions.notes: test al, 1 then jz jumps when AL is even.

instructions.name: Shift left (also SAL)
instructions.operation: Shifts the bits left; the top bit goes to CF and a 0 comes in at the bottom. Each shift multiplies by 2.
instructions.notes: Shift by 1 or by CL. The flags above are for a shift by 1. A shift by CL = 0 changes no flags; for counts above 1, OF is undefined.

instructions.name: Shift right (unsigned)
instructions.operation: Shifts the bits right; the bottom bit goes to CF and a 0 comes in at the top. Each shift divides an unsigned number by 2.
instructions.notes: For a shift by 1, OF is the original top bit. Counts as for SHL.

instructions.name: Shift right (signed)
instructions.operation: Shifts the bits right, copying the sign bit in at the top. Each shift divides a signed number by 2, rounding down.
instructions.notes: For a shift by 1, OF is cleared. Counts as for SHL.

instructions.name: Rotate left
instructions.operation: Rotates the bits left; the top bit moves to the bottom and is also copied to CF.
instructions.notes: Rotates by 1 or by CL. For a rotate by 1, OF is set when the top bit changed. A rotate by CL = 0 changes no flags; for counts above 1, OF is undefined.

instructions.name: Rotate right
instructions.operation: Rotates the bits right; the bottom bit moves to the top and is also copied to CF.
instructions.notes: Counts and OF as for ROL.

instructions.name: Rotate left through carry
instructions.operation: Rotates left through CF: the top bit goes to CF and the old CF comes in at the bottom.
instructions.notes: Counts and OF as for ROL.

instructions.name: Rotate right through carry
instructions.operation: Rotates right through CF: the bottom bit goes to CF and the old CF comes in at the top.
instructions.notes: Counts and OF as for ROL.

instructions.name: Jump
instructions.operation: Continues execution at the target: near (same segment) or far (new CS:IP), direct or through a register or memory.

instructions.name: Conditional jumps
instructions.operation: Jumps to a target within -128 to +127 bytes when the condition holds, otherwise continues with the next instruction.
instructions.notes: Unsigned comparisons: JB/JC/JNAE (CF=1), JAE/JNB/JNC (CF=0), JBE/JNA (CF=1 or ZF=1), JA/JNBE (CF=0 and ZF=0). Signed comparisons: JL/JNGE (SF<>OF), JGE/JNL (SF=OF), JLE/JNG (ZF=1 or SF<>OF), JG/JNLE (ZF=0 and SF=OF). Single flags: JE/JZ (ZF=1), JNE/JNZ (ZF=0), JS (SF=1), JNS (SF=0), JO (OF=1), JNO (OF=0), JP/JPE (PF=1), JNP/JPO (PF=0).

instructions.name: Jump if CX is zero
instructions.operation: Jumps when CX = 0 (short target).
instructions.notes: Often placed before a LOOP so a count of 0 skips the loop.

instructions.name: Loop
instructions.operation: CX = CX - 1; jumps when CX isn't 0 (short target).
instructions.notes: Decrementing CX here doesn't change the flags, unlike DEC.

instructions.name: Loop while equal (also LOOPZ)
instructions.operation: CX = CX - 1; jumps when CX isn't 0 and ZF = 1.

instructions.name: Loop while not equal (also LOOPNZ)
instructions.operation: CX = CX - 1; jumps when CX isn't 0 and ZF = 0.

instructions.name: Call a procedure
instructions.operation: Pushes the return address (IP, and CS for a far call) and jumps to the procedure.

instructions.name: Return from a procedure
instructions.operation: Pops IP (and CS for RETF). RET n also adds n to SP, removing n bytes of arguments.
instructions.notes: Use RETF to return from a far call.

instructions.name: Call an interrupt
instructions.operation: Pushes FLAGS, CS and IP, clears IF and TF, and jumps through the interrupt vector table.
instructions.notes: INT 21h calls DOS services and INT 20h ends the program; the help pages list the supported services. INTO calls interrupt 4 only when OF = 1.
instructions.probeSkipped: The interrupt router hands interrupts to the runtime's services, so a single CPU step doesn't show the CPU's own effect.

instructions.name: Return from an interrupt
instructions.operation: Pops IP, CS and FLAGS.
instructions.notes: Every flag takes the value of its bit in the popped word.

instructions.name: Move string (MOVSB, MOVSW)
instructions.operation: Copies the byte or word at DS:SI to ES:DI, then steps SI and DI by 1 or 2 (backwards when DF = 1).
instructions.notes: With REP it copies CX elements.

instructions.name: Load string (LODSB, LODSW)
instructions.operation: Loads AL or AX from DS:SI, then steps SI.

instructions.name: Store string (STOSB, STOSW)
instructions.operation: Stores AL or AX at ES:DI, then steps DI.
instructions.notes: rep stosb fills CX bytes with AL.

instructions.name: Compare strings (CMPSB, CMPSW)
instructions.operation: Compares the element at DS:SI with the one at ES:DI (flags as for CMP), then steps SI and DI.
instructions.notes: With REPE it stops at the first difference; with REPNE at the first match.

instructions.name: Scan string (SCASB, SCASW)
instructions.operation: Compares AL or AX with the element at ES:DI (flags as for CMP), then steps DI.
instructions.notes: repne scasb finds the first byte equal to AL.

instructions.name: Repeat prefixes (REP, REPE/REPZ, REPNE/REPNZ)
instructions.operation: Repeats the string instruction that follows while CX isn't 0, decrementing CX each time. REPE also stops when ZF = 0, REPNE when ZF = 1 (only CMPS and SCAS set ZF).
instructions.notes: The prefix itself changes no flags; a repeated CMPS or SCAS sets them as usual.

instructions.name: Clear carry
instructions.operation: CF = 0.

instructions.name: Set carry
instructions.operation: CF = 1.

instructions.name: Complement carry
instructions.operation: CF = not CF.

instructions.name: Clear direction
instructions.operation: DF = 0: string instructions step forward.

instructions.name: Set direction
instructions.operation: DF = 1: string instructions step backward.

instructions.name: Clear interrupt enable
instructions.operation: IF = 0.

instructions.name: Set interrupt enable
instructions.operation: IF = 1.

instructions.name: No operation
instructions.operation: Does nothing (it is XCHG AX, AX).

instructions.name: Halt
instructions.operation: Stops the processor. In Assembly Studio the program stops with a "halted" message.
instructions.probeSkipped: HLT ends execution; there is no following state to compare.

instructions.name: Wait for the coprocessor
instructions.operation: Without an 8087 coprocessor (as here) it does nothing.

instructions.name: Lock prefix
instructions.operation: Locks the bus for the next instruction on multiprocessor systems. Assembly Studio accepts and ignores it.

instructions.name: Segment override prefixes
instructions.operation: Makes the next instruction's memory operand use the given segment instead of its default (DS, or SS for addresses using BP).
instructions.notes: Written inside the brackets in NASM: mov al, [es:bx]. The destination of a string instruction is always ES:DI.
